merger_description:
CVC Capital Partners plc (together with its affiliates and subsidiaries, **CVC**), through Foxtrot US Bidco Inc, Foxtrot UK Bidco Limited and Foxtrot Denmark Bidco ApS (collectively, the **Purchasers**), entered into a transaction agreement with International Flavors & Fragrances Inc. (together with its direct and indirect subsidiaries, **IFF**) for the acquisition of c. 90% of the equity interests in its Food Ingredients business (the **Target Business**) (the **Acquisition**).

The Purchasers are indirectly controlled by funds or vehicles advised or managed by affiliates of CVC.

CVC is a global alternative investment manager focused on private equity, credit, infrastructure and secondaries, and includes CVC Capital Partners plc (**CVC plc**), each of its subsidiaries from time to time and the CVC Funds (defined below). CVC plc is listed on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange. As it relates to the CVC Network’s private equity activities, CVC plc indirectly, through certain of its subsidiaries from time to time, provides investment advice to and/or manages investments on behalf of certain funds and investment vehicles (the **CVC Funds**).

CVC holds interests in a number of companies active in a variety of industries around the world, including in financial services, chemicals, utilities, manufacturing, retailing and distribution, in Europe, the US and the Asia-Pacific region.

IFF is a creator and manufacturer of products for the food, beverage, health and biosciences and scent sectors. IFF maintains a global production footprint comprising 36 production sites, 17 application laboratories and 5 pilot plants across all major regions, with approximately 6,000 employees.

IFF’s Food Ingredients business develops, manufactures and sells ingredient solutions for the food and beverage industry. Its main product lines are developed across seven key operations: ingredient systems, protein solutions, emulsifiers, texturants, food inclusions, sweeteners, and food protection.

Post-completion of the Acquisition, CVC, through the Purchasers, will own a majority stake in, and have sole control over, the Target Business and hold a majority of the votes of the Board of Directors of the company that ultimately controls the Target Business at closing. IFF will retain a non-controlling minority stake of ~9.9% in the Target Business.

In Australia, the transferring Target Business entities will be Danisco Australia Pty Limited, Nutrition & Biosciences Australia Pty Ltd, Solae Australia Pty Limited, and Taura Natural Ingredients Holdings Pty Limited.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, the
notification waiver application in respect of CVC’s proposed
acquisition of the IRCA Group, and certain publicly available
information, and had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of
the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers
that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening
of competition given:
a. the parties’ combined share in the supply of MCC (for
pharmaceutical and food applications to customers) in
Australia is low and the increase in share of supply arising
from the Acquisition would be small
b. there are alternative suppliers of MCC (for both
pharmaceutical and food applications) to customers in
Australia
c. the parties’ combined share in the supply of food ingredient
solutions to customers in Australia (including the IRCA
Group’s share) is low, and the increase in share of supply
arising from the Acquisition would be small
d. there are alternative suppliers of food ingredient solutions to
customers in Australia
e. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
effects resulting from exclusionary conduct post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
